photos.title: Berdorf (LU), Werschrummschloeff -- 2015 -- 6230-4
photos.description: Labyrinth “Werschrummschloeff” in Berdorf, LuxembourgThe Werschrummschloeff, also known as Werschrummschlöff or Werschrummschlüff, is a fascinating rock labyrinth in the “Little Luxembourg Switzerland” near Berdorf in Luxembourg. This natural phenomenon consists of narrow, winding crevices and caves that were formed by thousands of years of erosion and are now a popular destination for hikers and nature lovers.The formation of Werschrummschloeff dates back to the Jurassic period around 200 million years ago, when the region was covered by a primeval sea. The special geological conditions led to the formation of the striking limestone formations that characterize the labyrinth today.

ImageDescription.value:
Labyrinth “Werschrummschloeff” in Berdorf, Luxembourg
The Werschrummschloeff, also known as Werschrummschlöff or Werschrummschlüff, is a fascinating rock labyrinth in the “Little Luxembourg Switzerland” near Berdorf in Luxembourg. This natural phenomenon consists of narrow, winding crevices and caves that were formed by thousands of years of erosion and are now a popular destination for hikers and nature lovers.
The formation of Werschrummschloeff dates back to the Jurassic period around 200 million years ago, when the region was covered by a primeval sea. The special geological conditions led to the formation of the striking limestone formations that characterize the labyrinth today.

photos.title: Quellacocha (Amazing Andean landscape with glacial lake) 23
photos.description: On the way to Huchuy Qosqo, the archaeological site, several Andean lakes appear while you hike up to your fate. The trailhead is the peasant community of Tambomachay; after walking 30 minutes, the majestic Apu Katunki receives on its mountain slope. At this point, it requires a mandatory greeting to the Apu Katunki, and thankfully, with everything on your path finally arriving at the mountain pass Katunki, go ahead to the small first lake that is relatively close to Quellachoca. This unknown lake maintains life for the Andean flora and fauna, such as a bunch of llamas and alpacas, as well as Andean birds like Huallatas, Puna Ibis, and more endemic species.
